title: MLX evaluation: distinguish graph construction, submission and readable completion
summary: At the pinned implementation, creating an array graph and marking it evaluated do not alone establish host-readable completion; eval and array waits provide separate completion boundaries.

software: ml-explore/mlx at bff10220c742907f0c68e55ff174aaea56f74e3d; later revisions require reinspection
conditions: Actual backend, streams, shapes/dtypes and evaluation boundary are recorded.
CPU, Metal and CUDA source paths are distinguished; discovery or catalog placement is not runtime qualification.

claims.description: Array construction retains its primitive and inputs. async_eval submits unscheduled outputs; eval waits on existing output events or the eval_impl synchronizer.
is_available distinguishes evaluated arrays with unfinished events from available arrays. array::eval evaluates unscheduled arrays and otherwise waits.

downstream_impact: An InferRSI transfer hypothesis for a matching MLX workload; no implicit vLLM, MLX-LM or other engine compatibility is claimed.
recommendations: Identify the exact eval, stream synchronization or host-read boundary before interpreting submission time as completed work.
validation_plan: On a separately authorized matching build, retain identical inputs and compare async submission timing with an explicit completion boundary and checked results.
limitations: This card addresses read readiness, not cross-stream dependency wiring, allocator policy or model performance.
Source map originally inspected 2026-10-21; these bounded implementation ranges were rechecked 2026-10-23. No MLX backend test or performance measurement was run.
